en.title: GTA 6 and Fable Trailers Lead a Week of Big Gaming Reveals
en.summary: The gaming world is abuzz as Rockstar finally unveiled the first extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6, while Fable offered a glimpse into its vast world. This week's trailer drops have set a new bar for anticipation.
en.body:
This past week has been an absolute spectacle for trailer enthusiasts, with **Rockstar Games** finally dropping the long-awaited extended look at **Grand Theft Auto 6**. After enduring a series of leaks, the 27-minute trailer confirmed what many suspected: this is shaping up to be one of the most ambitious titles in gaming history. The sheer scope and detail shown have left players stunned, eager to dive back into the vibrant, chaotic world of Vice City. The game is slated for release on **PlayStation 5** and **Xbox Series X|S** on November 19.

But **Grand Theft Auto 6** wasn't the only major reveal. **Gamescom Opening Night Live** also delivered a cascade of new footage, most notably for the highly anticipated **Fable** reboot. While there's plenty of new gameplay to explore, 18 minutes of quest gameplay in the sprawling city of Bowerstone stole the show. The sheer density of interactive elements, with over 130 homes and 30 businesses players can enter, hints at a world brimming with personality and emergent gameplay. The brief glimpses of combat and character interactions suggest a return to the series' beloved charm, with a touch of modern polish. **Fable** is scheduled to launch on **PS5**, **Xbox Series X|S**, and **PC** on February 23, 2027.

Beyond these titans, the week also saw **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt** receiving a significant update with a remastered version and the new 'Songs of the Past' DLC. This expansion promises to add new quests, characters, and a fresh storyline, further enriching an already critically acclaimed title. These updates ensure that **The Witcher 3** continues to be a relevant and engaging experience for both veteran players and newcomers alike.

## The Hype Train is Officially Leaving the Station

For fans, this week's trailer drops represent more than just previews; they are the culmination of years of speculation and desire. The **GTA 6** trailer, in particular, has reignited discussions about the future of open-world gaming, with players dissecting every frame for clues and easter eggs. The return of **Fable** also strikes a chord, tapping into nostalgia for a series that defined a generation of role-playing games on the Xbox. The sheer volume of content revealed suggests a busy period ahead for gamers, with major releases and substantial updates on the horizon. The community is buzzing with theories and excitement, ready to experience these worlds firsthand.

## What's Next

With **GTA 6** targeting a November 19 release and **Fable** set for February 23, 2027, players have immediate and long-term horizons to look forward to. Further details on **The Witcher 3's** DLC content are expected to emerge, keeping the world of Geralt of Rivia alive and well. The sheer anticipation for these titles suggests they will be major players in the gaming landscape for years to come.

content_raw: It’s been a huge week for trailers, specifically for games (though the entertainment front hardly took the week off). Of course, the big headline from this week is GTA 6. (Did your Netflix break when you tried to log on to watch the Extended Look right when it dropped?) But gamescom has also been busy shelling out one trailer after another since Tuesday’s Opening Night Live . What’s included here is merely a tiny smattering of the biggest hits; you can peruse all of them — there are currently 187 — at your leisure on IGN’s YouTube channel . Here are the trailers you should watch from this week (and here’s what you missed last week ). Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look In the trailer event to end all trailer events, Rockstar finally dropped a long 27-minute look at the most anticipated game of the decade after enduring a series of brutal leaks (that seems like it might also have been a crypto scheme ). What else is there to say that my esteemed colleagues have not already ? Obviously, it looks insane. GTA 6 is coming out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19. Fable quest gameplay There’s tons of new footage from Fable that you can check out from gamescom — plus, read our preview — but I was particularly drawn to these 18 minutes of quest gameplay that takes the Hero through the massive and gorgeous Bowerstone (130 homes and 30 businesses and you can go in all of them??? ), highlights some character interactions (I also would have thrown the beer at Humphry), and shows off a tiny bit of combat (I scrubbed back on shooting that one thug in the knee with an arrow like three times, very good). Fable releases on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC on February 23, 2027. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered + Songs of the Past DLC The Witcher 3 got a twofer out of gamescom 2026: a remaster trailer (which will be free for players who already own the game ) and the Songs of the Past DLC. Any excuse to hang out with Geralt another time is cool in my book. The Remaster, of course, looks super slick, but Songs of the Past especially has me intrigued with the freakiness of Letten. The Witcher 3 Remaster is available September 29; the Songs of the Past DLC does not currently have a release window. Final Fantasy VII Revelation gameplay trailer The Weapons! Are! Here! The FFVII Revelation look out of gamescom — the first since SGF — was fairly short, focusing mostly on those giant monsters, but it did show off more of the aerial and submarine combat that’s coming in the trilogy-ending FFVII remake. Hell yeah, brother. Final Fantasy VII Revelation comes out in spring 2027. No Law No Law was a fun gamescom reveal — it’s an FPS where you play as the field-tested, now peace-seeking Grey Harker. I don’t know much else about what it’s actually about, but I do know that this tongue-in-cheek, cyber-noir, gadget-driven stealth game that also lets you blow some heads off seems pretty dang fun.
